name: Carolingian Empire
summary: Charlemagne’s Frankish empire, which united much of western Europe. It brought a revival of learning (the Carolingian Renaissance) and later split into what became France and Germany.

location.value: France, Germany, the Low Countries, northern Italy and beyond.

terrain.value: Plains, forests and river valleys of the Rhine, Seine, Loire and Po.

climate.value: Temperate, with occasional harsh winters and failed harvests.

resources.value: Farmland, forests, silver mines and salt.

disasters.value: Famines, such as in 792–793, when Charlemagne set grain price limits.

urbanisation.value: Few large towns; most people lived on rural estates and around monasteries.

migration.value: Viking and Saracen raids increased in the 9th century.

economicBase.value: Agriculture on large manors worked by serfs.

tradeRoutes.value: River trade and North Sea trade through Dorestad and Quentovic.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: A reformed silver penny (denarius): 240 pennies to the pound, a system used in Britain until 1971.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

inequality.value: Nobles and the church owned most land; most people were unfree peasants.

governmentType.value: Monarchy under an emperor, crowned by the Pope in 800.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

keyRulers.value: Charlemagne (800–814), Louis the Pious, Charles the Fat (last).

succession.value: The empire was divided among sons, following Frankish custom.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

institutions.value: Counts governed regions; royal envoys (missi dominici) inspected them; capitularies were royal decrees.

stability.value: A civil war from 840 to 843 among Charlemagne’s grandsons.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry among Louis the Pious’s sons.

armyAndTech.value: Armoured mounted warriors summoned from the nobility each spring.

majorWars.value: Saxon Wars (772–804), conquest of the Lombards (774), wars against the Avars.

territoryChange.value: About 1.2 million km² in the 9th century; divided at Verdun in 843.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with the Pope; rivals of Byzantium, Umayyad Spain and the Vikings.

inventions.value: Carolingian minuscule, a clear handwriting that led to modern lowercase letters.

scienceEducation.value: Palace and monastery schools; scholars such as Alcuin of York copied classical texts.

openness.value: Revived Roman and Christian learning, drawing scholars from England, Ireland, Spain and Italy.

religion.value: Latin Christianity under the Church of Rome.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

languageWriting.value: Latin for church and government; Romance and Germanic languages spoken.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

artsArchitecture.value: The Palatine Chapel at Aachen and illuminated manuscripts.

socialStructure.value: Nobles, clergy, free peasants and serfs.

sharedIdentity.value: Christianity and loyalty to the emperor.

neighbours.value: Byzantium, the Saxons, Avars, Danes and Umayyad al-Andalus.

ideasReligions.value: Spread Christianity among the Saxons and others, often by force.

riseSignals.value: Charlemagne’s conquests and his coronation on 25 December 800.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

declineSignals.value: Division among his grandsons (843) and Viking raids.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Carolingian Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); McKitterick, Charlemagne (2008)

outcome.value: Dissolved in 888. Successors: West Francia, East Francia, Middle Francia.

sources.value: Einhard’s Life of Charlemagne, charters. Checked against Wikipedia (“Carolingian Empire”).

overallCertainty.value: Good. Based on Einhard, annals and charters.

knownFor.label: Carolingian minuscule
knownFor.note: Handwriting that led to modern lowercase letters.

knownFor.label: Charlemagne
knownFor.note: Crowned emperor by the Pope in 800.
